independent_audit: All nine supplied main pages and 11 matched SI pages read and independently audited. The canonical records and reader, molecular/stock references, 21 operation illustrations and symbolic source sample contexts passed separate scoped audits. One synthesis route, seven supporting preparation/acquisition procedures and eleven observation records remain distinct. Nine paired comparison contexts do not establish independent replicate counts or shared physical aliquots. Source inconsistencies and missing conditions remain explicit. No current QD atomic coordinates or exact structure–recipe training pair is admitted.

Complete supplied main and matched SI reviewed; source conflicts and reference-versus-measured structure limits remain explicit.

No isomer or water-content assay is supplied.

items.title: Hot injection and sequential purification
items.text: The source compares three ligand ratios, three washing ratios and three growth temperatures in separate experimental families. Each of the nine condition options preserves the other two source-fixed parameters. They are not a full Cartesian design or nine identified physical batches. The first centrifugation retains the precipitate; the second retains the supernatant. Growth dwell, wash amounts and storage conditions remain unreported.

items.title: Growth-temperature diffraction, PL, TEM and distributions
items.text: Panels a–c show diffraction, time-resolved PL and normalized PL for growth at 25, 50 and 100 °C. OAm:OA is 1:3 and washing is 1:20 acetonitrile:toluene. Panels d–f are TEM images with 20 nm bars; the 100 °C inset labels d(002) = 6.38 Å. Panels g–i report mean dimensions of 7.6 ± 2.4, 9.5 ± 1.6 and 10.4 ± 1.1 nm, with histogram FWHM values 5.7, 3.7 and 2.7 nm. The ± statistic is undefined. The 25 °C diffraction marks PbI2 and δ-FAPbI3 alongside α-phase assignments.

items.title: Variable-temperature PL
items.text: Measure PL from 80 to 430 K. Fit spectra with Lorentzian functions and extract PL peak energy, FWHM and intensity. The observed trend changes are assigned to γ-tetragonal-1 → β-tetragonal-2 at 140 K and β → α-cubic at 250 K. These are source interpretations supported by optical/Raman trends, not variable-temperature coordinate refinements on the QDs.

items.text: At 250 K the energy slope changes to 3.97 × 10−4 eV/K and FWHM slope to 1.69 × 10−4 eV/K. PL intensity increases up to 350 K. The source attributes this to improved cubic order, lower defect density and facet-dependent recombination; it does not measure carrier mobility directly.

items.title: Raman phase interpretation
items.text: Peaks around 120 and 250 cm−1 are assigned to I–Pb–I stretching and FA+ vibrations by comparison to cited studies. The 120 cm−1 peak shifts blue from 80 to 140 K then red above 140 K. FWHM is described as constant from 80 to 130 K with an abrupt change near 140 K. The prose mistakenly calls the Raman graphic Figure S1; its actual caption is S2.

items.title: Prior Raman ambiguity
items.text: Prior assignments of 111 cm−1 to δ and 135 cm−1 to α are contrasted with a study assigning 135 cm−1 to laser-induced PbO2 degradation, and reports of 96/111 cm−1 for α. These are cited contexts, not measured current PbO2 or δ contamination. Reference titles for some FA-mode comparisons concern methylammonium perovskites; preserve the stated comparison without validating an exact mode identity.

items.title: PL stability at 350 K
items.text: Figure S3 compares the 300 K spectrum with 350 K spectra at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 and 210 min. The normalized intensity fit is PL_Intensity(t) = −0.026(t) + 1, with t in hours. This is a slight observed decline despite the main description highly stable; no absolute PL quantum yield is provided.

operations.description: Measure PL from 80 to 430 K. Fit spectra with Lorentzian functions and extract PL peak energy, FWHM and intensity. The observed trend changes are assigned to γ-tetragonal-1 → β-tetragonal-2 at 140 K and β → α-cubic at 250 K. These are source interpretations supported by optical/Raman trends, not variable-temperature coordinate refinements on the QDs.

items.title: Ligand mechanism interpretation
items.text: The authors associate excess OAm with protonated OAm+ replacing FA+ and disrupting the lattice, insufficient OA with reduced FA-oleate formation, and excess OA with hindered growth and dissolution in washing solvent. These are mechanistic explanations, not measured occupancies, solution structures or reaction stoichiometries.

items.title: Phase and emission model
items.text: The scheme shows γ-tetragonal to β-tetragonal at 140 K, α-cubic at 250 K, PL enhancement through 350 K, then an expanded α schematic. Facet-dependent trap suppression, strain relief, exciton delocalization and bright-state activation are explanatory hypotheses. Source-drawn atomic-looking icons do not provide recoverable sample coordinates.

items.title: Source conclusion
items.text: The source concludes that optimized ligand, purification and growth conditions yield approximately 10.4 nm QDs, roughly 150 ns lifetimes and low-index diffraction features, with γ→β→α optical/Raman transitions and PL enhancement up to 350 K. Application to solar cells is prospective; this study supplies no fabricated solar-cell recipe or measured device efficiency.
